entries.subject: Ymir published convex-model envelope
entries.finding: Denk and Mottola (2013), EP7.2 and the author’s numeric table constrain an approximate triangular body with equatorial edges 20, 24 and 25 km and an adopted 8 km polar semiaxis. The selected elliptical polar-cap law is assumed. The separate 9.6 km photometric radius is not used to rescale those dimensions; no original inversion mesh is claimed.

entries.subject: Original Ymir convex inversion mesh
entries.finding: The actual linked 619_Ymi_5_Shape.obj endpoint returned HTTP 404 during the documented survey, consistent with its unavailable status on the page. The authored approximation is not presented as a recovered native model.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Ymir mesh with model frame, method and reuse documentation can be compared with the approximation.

entries.subject: Ymir spectroscopy route
entries.finding: Published disk-integrated colors do not establish a spatial color map. The author notes possible UVIS/VIMS observations, but the survey did not qualify an extracted spectrum. Instrument observations alone do not establish an interpretable spectral lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A released interpretable spectrum can support a chart; a registered spatial product would be needed for a surface lens.

entries.subject: Terrain and geology route
entries.finding: No resolved DEM, registered geology or mapped composition product was qualified; model facets do not establish terrain.
entries.revisitWhen: A body-specific registered terrain, geology or composition release can be reviewed.

entries.subject: Cassini ISS Ymir light-curve data
entries.finding: The author’s multi-observation table 619_Ymi_4_LC_Paper1.txt and 2008 series 619_ymi_4_lc064.txt were identified as observation-chart candidates. Their disk-integrated samples are not registered surface pixels, and no chart is selected.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation view is in scope and the original time-series samples are validated for units, cadence and uncertainties.
